topic: Light and power during a blackout without panic-buying

content.hook: POV: lights go out, your phone is at 12%

slides.title: *POV:* lights out, phone at 12%
slides.body: Blackout lighting and power, without panic-buying.

slides.title: Start with what you *already own*
slides.body: Torches, headlamps, spare batteries. Gather them in one spot before buying anything.

slides.title: One *light* per person
slides.body: A headlamp keeps your hands free. Keep it where you can find it in the dark.

slides.title: Go easy on *candles*
slides.body: LED torches are safer. If you do use a candle, never leave it unattended.

slides.title: Save phone *battery* for messages
slides.body: Keep a power bank charged. Use low-power mode and send short texts, not long calls.

slides.title: A calm plan beats a *panic* cart

content.caption:
POV: lights go out, your phone is at 12%. Here's blackout lighting and power planning without panic-buying.

You don't need a car full of gear. Start small:
• Gather the torches, headlamps and batteries you already own in one place.
• Aim for one light per person.
• Pick LED over candles. Fewer fire risks.
• Keep a power bank charged and save phone battery for short messages.
